Maasland Agro Processing BV is carrying six open invoices with a single client, Solvenza Trade Credit (CL03), totalling €1,267,900. One of those, INV000340, is 55 days past due for €140,000 on 60-day terms; the remaining €1.13M is not yet due. There is no settled invoice history on file, so the payment agent records the trend as "insufficient_history" and cannot say whether late payment is typical or exceptional here. Separately, a Continental Trade Wire report of 26 October 2025 said the company cut its Zwolle unit from three shifts to one on weak order inflow in Food Processing, released contract workers and slowed material procurement; the company confirmed only a "temporary realignment of production". Total open exposure sits close to the single €1.38M credit line, and only one insurer covers this buyer.

The score is 66.9, placing the buyer in High Risk with a PD of 0.6396. The trace is 0.65 x 90.0 (payment, 55 DPD) + 0.35 x 23.9 (news) = 66.9. The payment raw of 90.0 is set by worst-line DPD alone and treats the whole relationship as if it were 55 DPD, even though only €140,000 of the €1,267,900 is actually delinquent. The news component is a severity 4 capacity_cut article, now 334 days old and decayed from a base of 45.0 to 23.86. The adjudicator's assessment is "agree_with_caveats": the band is directionally defensible but rests on thin foundations. Note the band-determining sensitivity — payment alone gives 0.65 x 90.0 = 58.5, below the 60 High Risk cutoff, so the 8.4 weighted news points from this single, largely single-sourced article are what move the buyer from Watch to High Risk. The concentration risk flagged by the payment agent is not captured anywhere in the formula.

The recommendation for Solvenza Trade Credit (LIM0009) is REDUCE: cut the current limit of €1,380,000 to a revised limit of €1,267,900, on the basis of cutting to the limit where expected loss meets the 25% appetite against a PD of 0.6396 versus a PD target of 0.25. Expected loss falls from €637,713 to €585,911. Maximum liability does not bind. In practice this trims headroom to the level of exposure already outstanding rather than reducing live risk, so it should be paired with the verification steps below.

Two things would lift this. First, confirm the status of INV000340 — if the €140,000 clears or proves to be a one-off dispute or administrative delay rather than a structural deterioration, the payment raw of 90.0 loses its basis; building up settled invoice history would also close the data-quality gap that currently prevents any trend analysis. Second, refresh the news signal: no corroborating or follow-up coverage appears in the evidence in the 334 days since publication, so it is unclear whether the capacity cut persisted, reversed, or simply went unmonitored.
